newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM demands resignation of defence minister.
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM demands resignation of defence minister.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Wednesday he was seeking the resignation of his defence minister, accusing him of shady fuel deals for the army.
The fight against corruption is high on the agenda in Latvia, which quit the former Soviet Union in 1991.
The small Baltic state wants to present a clean image to the West as it aims for European Union membership.
"I have demanded the resignation of Defence Minister Andrejs Krastinsh as I have lost confidence in him," Shkele told a news conference.
His request has to be approved by the president.
Krastinsh went to Denmark on Wednesday for a meeting of Baltic state, Danish, German and Polish defence ministers and he was not available for comment on Shkele's accusations.
Shkele refused to give more details but said the fuel deals violated state procurement rules and that any misuse of state funds would not be tolerated by his government.

"The fighting of corruption has to become one of the main jobs of the state and all people responsible for the use of state funds must be aware that their activities will be scrutinised very closely," Shkele said.
Shkele, a no-nonsense businessman without party affiliation, is widely regarded as a staunch reformer and the only glue binding Latvia's unwieldy eight-party coalition.

Krastinsh's party is one of the junior members of the coalition but it recently agreed to merge with the second-largest party in the government. The coalition has around two-thirds of the 100-seat parliament.
